title: Keep CI wall time history readable across dashboard updates

intentCoverage.report:
**Caught.** Exactly one plausible fault reached and failed the existing assertion protecting the selected story promise.

- **Promise and revision.** An already-open prior frontend can parse the updated default CI history response, retaining measured builds and understandable timing-basis gaps without reloading. Story `SEED-305#keep-ci-wall-time-history-readable-across-dashboard-updates`, source `.planning/seeds/SEED-305-ci-wall-time-history-across-dashboard-updates.md`, completed plan `.planning/slice-plans/581-keep-ci-wall-time-history-readable-across-dashboard-updates/PLAN.md`, at revision `4006ba5558633f56ce3881e2a819bf85dccca8b8`.
- **Single fault.** In `dashboard/server/intentCiHistoryRead.ts:179`, replaced `entries: readableHistoryEntries(historyEntries(history), read?.gapReasons)` with `entries: historyEntries(history)`. This bypassed compatible final-reason projection on the unscoped local HTTP response. No other product change, fixture change, or assertion change was made.
- **Fixture and intended assertion.** The existing MakeMe fixture in `dashboard/backend-tests/intent/ci-history-reader-compatibility.spec.ts:22` retains one landing for each of the 11 current final reasons and one measured build of 120000 ms. Its independently frozen prior deployed reader is from `49367c2e4`. The intended assertion is `previousHistorySchema.parse(await answer(query))` at line 100; subsequent assertions protect measured points, gap count, compatible `not-recorded` reason and prior understandable wording.
- **Command and setup.** Prepared a detached isolated scratch checkout at the selected revision and ran locked `npm ci`. Every run used `caffeinate -s -i npm run test:dashboard -- backend-tests/intent/ci-history-reader-compatibility.spec.ts --workers=1`, with distinct external proof-record destinations. Actual host observations showed AC power and 16 CPUs; one-minute load was 4.06 during setup, 10.65 before the faulty run, and 10.37 before restoration verification. No full suite, retries, sleeps, or timeout changes were used.
- **Observed reach and result.** Baseline completed both selected tests with one passing attempt each. With the fault, the compatibility test's actual default HTTP answer passed its existing status-200 assertion, then failed the intended frozen-reader parse with a Zod final-reason rejection at `entries[8].reason`. Entry 8 is the fixture's `timing-basis` landing, the current vocabulary's only final reason absent from the frozen prior reader. The changed response therefore reached the prior reader and reproduced whole-response rejection; this was not merely fault execution. The neighboring capability-negotiation test still passed. The single deliberate faulty run exited 1; baseline and restored commands exited 0.
- **Restoration and cleanup.** A signal-aware `finally` handler restored the exact original source after the fault. Before and after the restored run, selected HEAD, clean Git status, and SHA-256 hashes of the response source, owning test, frozen reader, and lockfile matched the recorded pre-probe state. The restored command completed both tests with one passing attempt each. The clean scratch checkout and its dependencies were removed safely. The coordinator's checkout was never edited, switched, stashed, or reset. Proof records, state comparisons, and the fault report remain outside all worktrees under `/tmp/seed305-intent-coverage-*`; the report is `/tmp/seed305-intent-coverage.txt`.
- **Test runtime.** 16812.351 ms total (measured from the maintained runner's terminal `durationMs` records): baseline 5787.112 ms; deliberate fault 5379.982 ms; restored 5645.257 ms. These are runner durations, not invocation elapsed.
- **Human effort.** Unavailable: no separate human-effort timing was recorded; zero effort is not inferred.
- **Agent effort.** Unavailable: no separate active-agent time or token-usage measure was exposed for this invocation; invocation elapsed is not substituted.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 210362 ms (measured), from 1794360469000 to 1794360679362 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.
